The kimchi ferment is a succession, not a single culture. Early on,
Leuconostoc species dominate — they tolerate cold and start working in
the fridge. Later Weissella and Lactobacillus take over as the acid
climbs.

This is why kimchi develops in stages rather than all at once: what
you taste on day three is not what you taste in week three. The
community replaces itself as the environment turns more acidic.

Salt levels around 2-3% keep the vegetables crisp and select for the
lab community over spoilage organisms. Gochugaru is mostly about
flavour and colour; the preservation is the salt and the cold.
